newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK 1996 trade deficit shrinks, seen stable in 1997.
newsitem.headline: HK 1996 trade deficit shrinks, seen stable in 1997.

text.p: Hong Kong's trade deficit shrank slightly in 1996, and analysts said on Thursday that the deficit was likely to remain at a similar level in 1997.

The Census and Statistics Department said Hong Kong had a provisional trade deficit of HK$137.7 billion (US$17.65 million) last year, down 6.3 percent from the previous year, as exports edged up four percent against a three percent gain in imports.
The December deficit stood at HK$14.7 billion versus HK$12.4 billion in the year-ago month.

A government spokesman noted export growth had been considerably slower last year than in 1995, but analysts said an expected pick-up in exports this year was likely to lead to a similar or slightly smaller deficit in 1997.
"The trade deficit (forecast for 1997) is almost the same as '96, but slightly smaller," said W.I. Carr economist Craig Chan.
Total exports are likely to grow this year with an expected increase in re-exports from China, whose economy is improving, said Shamus Mok, chief economist at Bank of East Asia.

Imports would also rise this year due to a better consumer market but its growth would be limited by a fall in the imports of capital goods for Hong Kong's new airport, which is nearing completion, he said.
Chan said he expected "quite strong growth" in total exports backed by a pick-up in domestic exports, although Mok anticipated continued sluggishness in domestic exports.
Lower prices on Japanese goods resulting from a weak yen would also restrict growth in the value of imports, Mok added.
"When the total exports grow and total imports do not grow so much, the trade balance may maintain at this very reasonable level," he said.
Chan also said growth of imports would be slightly lower than of exports, resulting in a slightly lower trade deficit.
Last year, total exports grew four percent to HK$1,397.92 billion. Re-exports rose 6.6 percent to HK$1,185.76 billion, but domestic exports fell 8.4 percent to HK$212.16 billion.
Imports rose three percent to HK$1,535.58 billion.

The government spokesman said export growth was curbed last year by factors including a slow-down in import demand in some major markets such as the United States and China, the global oversupply of electronic products, and the strength of the U.S. dollar to which the local currency is pegged.

But retained imports of captial goods, raw materials and semi-manufactured goods recorded some rises in recent months, suggesting a possible pick-up in production for export in coming months, he said.
